title: AI ticket deflection: resolve common issues, hand off the rest | Pylon
summary: Pylon's guide to AI ticket deflection for B2B: how agents resolve routine issues, hand off complex ones with context, and learn from escalations.
body_markdown:
**Short answer:** AI ticket deflection works best when you stop counting deflections and start asking a better question for each issue: should the agent resolve it, or hand it off? Agents should resolve routine questions your content already answers, and hand off anything that needs judgment, account access, or engineering, with the context gathered so a person can act fast. Then use every handoff to improve the agent. In Pylon, agents investigate issues before your team opens them, so handoffs arrive with the account, related issues, and a draft reply.


## What is AI ticket deflection?


AI ticket deflection is when an AI agent answers a customer's question so a person doesn't have to. Older deflection meant pointing customers to help articles and hoping they stopped asking. Agentic support goes further: the agent can answer, collect information, take action, or pass the issue to your team with an investigation already started.


In B2B, "deflect" is the wrong goal on its own. A deflected question that comes back angry next week isn't a win. What you want is the right outcome for each issue.


## Can AI agents resolve common issues and escalate complex ones?


Yes. A well-set-up agent resolves routine questions from your knowledge base and docs, and escalates the rest according to rules you define. In Pylon, Support Agent works like a teammate you assign issues to, manually or with triggers, and when it can't answer, it follows your escalation workflow and reassigns the issue ([Pylon docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/agents/support-agent/deploy) ).


Here's how we think about the split:


Issue type Example (B2B) Agent should What the person gets on handoff


How-to answered in your docs "How do I add a user to our workspace?" Resolve Nothing needed


Plan or policy question "Does our plan include SSO?" Resolve if plan data is connected, otherwise hand off The account's plan and the relevant policy


Information collection "Our export is failing" Collect details first (workspace, steps, error), then hand off A complete report instead of a back-and-forth


Account-specific behavior "Why did this team get deleted?" Investigate, then hand off with findings Log lines, timestamps, and a draft reply


Likely bug "This broke after last week's release" Hand off with context Related issues, open bugs, and code context


Contract, billing dispute, or renewal risk "We want to discuss our renewal" Hand off right away The account history and owner


## What does a good handoff look like?


A good handoff means the person who picks up the issue doesn't start from zero. It should arrive with what the customer is trying to do, what happened in earlier conversations, whether you've seen the issue before, and which bugs or product behavior might be relevant.


Agents investigate issues before your team opens them. On our own team, that means the hard ones arrive pre-investigated. One example: a customer asks when a team with a specific ID was deleted. The agent finds the ID, runs the search, pulls the relevant log lines and timestamps, and drafts a reply. What used to be a 30-minute investigation now takes about 2 minutes to review and approve ([How Pylon adopted Agentic Support](https://www.usepylon.com/ebooks/how-pylon-adopted-agentic-support) ).


## How much can AI deflection reduce support volume?


It depends on your mix, so measure it on your own issues rather than trusting a headline number. Before our own rollout, an AI agent resolved routine questions that made up around half of our incoming issues, but those accounted for only about 10% of our support team's time. The hard issues were where the time went.


That's why we pair resolution with investigation. Comparing the 4 weeks before rollout (May 4 to 31, 2026) with the 4 weeks after (June 8 to July 5, 2026), our median first response time fell 72%, from 19.4 to 5.3 minutes, while volume grew 3% ([How Pylon adopted Agentic Support](https://www.usepylon.com/ebooks/how-pylon-adopted-agentic-support) ).


## How do AI support agents learn from resolved issues and find knowledge base gaps?


They compare what the agent said with what your team actually did, then propose fixes. In Pylon, Improvements looks at resolved escalations, compares the teammate's answer with the agent's, and reads customer thumbs up and down. Where a real resolution backs it up, it proposes a change: new guidance, a new or updated Skill, or a knowledge base article ([Pylon docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/agents/support-agent/monitor-and-iterate/improve) ).


- **Missing content** keeps a queue of issues your team marked as needing a new or updated article. On Advanced and Enterprise, it also groups the questions your docs don't cover into topics, once you've logged 300 issues ([Pylon docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/knowledge-base/missing-content) ).
- **Backtesting** runs your agent against real past issues before it reaches a customer, so you can see where it would have replied and where it would have escalated. That shows you exactly where the resolve vs hand off line sits before you go live ([Pylon docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/agents/support-agent/test) ).
- Every proposal links to the issues behind it, and customer-facing articles, Skill changes, and guidance changes wait for your review.


## How do you measure AI deflection the right way?


Track outcomes, not just deflections:


Metric What it tells you


Resolution rate Share of assigned issues the agent closed without a handoff


Handoff rate and reason Where the agent stops, and why


Reopen or follow-up rate Whether "resolved" really meant resolved


First response time and SLA attainment Whether customers hear back faster


Time to resolve handed-off issues Whether handoffs actually save your team time


CSAT on agent replies Whether customers were happy with the answer


## How do you roll it out?


1. **Audit last month's issues.** Sort them into the rows of the table above.
2. **Fix your content.** Close the biggest gaps before the agent goes live.
3. **Write escalation rules and Skills.** Decide what the agent must always hand off.
4. **Backtest, then deploy to a slice.** Start with one channel or a set of issue types.
5. **Review improvements weekly.** Start with proposals that have the most evidence.


## How much does AI deflection cost?


It depends on the pricing model. Some vendors charge per outcome or per automated resolution, so cost grows with volume. Pylon doesn't charge per issue: Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month, on an annual contract, and agentic features run on credits ([Pylon pricing](https://www.usepylon.com/pricing) ). For current competitor prices, see[how much B2B support software costs](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-b2b-support-software-is-priced) . For how the agents compare, see[the best AI agents for B2B support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/best-ai-agents-b2b-support-2026) .


## FAQ


**Can AI agents resolve common issues and escalate complex ones?**


Yes. Agents resolve routine questions your content answers and escalate the rest by rules you set. In Pylon, Support Agent follows your escalation workflow and reassigns the issue when it can't answer.


**How do AI support agents learn from resolved issues?**


They compare the agent's reply with how your team resolved the issue and propose fixes. In Pylon, Improvements proposes guidance changes, Skills, or knowledge base articles, each linked to the issues behind it.


**How do you find knowledge base gaps?**


Look at the questions your docs don't answer. Pylon's Missing content page keeps a queue of issues marked as needing an article, and on Advanced and Enterprise it groups gaps into topics.


**What's the difference between deflection and resolution?**


Deflection means a person didn't have to answer. Resolution means the customer's problem was actually solved. Track reopen rates to tell them apart.


**How much does Pylon cost?**


Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month, on an annual contract. Enterprise is a custom quote, and agentic features run on credits.


**What's a good ticket deflection rate?**


There's no reliable benchmark across industries, because it depends on your mix of issues. Measure resolution and reopen rates on your own issues. On Pylon's own team, routine questions were about half of incoming issues but only about 10% of the support team's time.


**Do I need to replace my existing help desk to use AI deflection?**


Not always. Some AI agents plug into the help desk you already run, and escalations land back there. Pylon is the help desk itself, so teams switch to Pylon to replace their help desk. If you only want to add an AI layer to your current help desk, Pylon isn't built for that.
